findings.evidence: The proof’s sole use is `hnn i (x + 1)` inside the downward-closure argument.
findings.fix: Replace `hnn : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ P i j` with `hnn : ∀ j, 0 ≤ P i j` and specialize global nonnegativity at call sites.
findings.issue: `lt_tableauEntry_iff` assumes nonnegativity of every entry although its fixed-row statement only needs `∀ j, 0 ≤ P i j`.

findings.evidence: For `n = 0`, `P i n = P i 0 = 0` by `entry_eq_zero_of_le (Nat.zero_le i)`, contradicting `0 ≤ c < P i n`; `hn` is otherwise used only in `Nat.sub_add_cancel hn`.
findings.fix: Remove `hn`; handle `n = 0` by rewriting `P i 0` with `entry_eq_zero_of_le`, then run the existing argument in the successor case.
findings.issue: `tableauEntry_lt` unnecessarily requires `hn : 0 < n`; its hypothesis `(c : ℤ) < P i n` already rules out `n = 0`.

summary: Two counting lemmas retain assumptions stronger than their proofs and statements require.
